cudaEnableDefault.doc: Default search mode for driver symbols.

cudaEnableLegacyStream.doc: Search for legacy versions of driver symbols.

cudaEnablePerThreadDefaultStream.doc: Search for per-thread versions of driver symbols.

cudaErrorAddressOfConstant.doc: This indicated that the user has taken the address of a constant variable, which was forbidden up until the CUDA 3.1 release.

cudaErrorAlreadyAcquired.doc: This indicates that a resource has already been acquired.

cudaErrorAlreadyMapped.doc: This indicates that the resource is already mapped.

cudaErrorArrayIsMapped.doc: This indicates that the specified array is currently mapped and thus cannot be destroyed.

cudaErrorAssert.doc:
An assert triggered in device code during kernel execution.

The device cannot be used again. All existing allocations are invalid. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorCallRequiresNewerDriver.doc:
This indicates that the API call requires a newer CUDA driver than the one currently installed.

Users should install an updated NVIDIA CUDA driver to allow the API call to succeed.

cudaErrorCapturedEvent.doc: The operation is not permitted on an event which was last recorded in a capturing stream.

cudaErrorCdpNotSupported.doc: This error indicates, that the program is using CUDA Dynamic Parallelism, but the current configuration, like MPS, does not support it.

cudaErrorCdpVersionMismatch.doc: This error indicates, that the program contains an unsupported interaction between different versions of CUDA Dynamic Parallelism.

cudaErrorCompatNotSupportedOnDevice.doc:
This error indicates that the system was upgraded to run with forward compatibility but the visible hardware detected by CUDA does not support this configuration.

Refer to the compatibility documentation for the supported hardware matrix or ensure that only supported hardware is visible during initialization via the CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES environment variable.

cudaErrorContained.doc:
This indicates that an exception occurred on the device that is now contained by the GPU’s error containment capability.

Common causes are - a. Certain types of invalid accesses of peer GPU memory over nvlink b. Certain classes of hardware errors This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorContextIsDestroyed.doc: This error indicates that the context current to the calling thread has been destroyed using ::cuCtxDestroy, or is a primary context which has not yet been initialized.

cudaErrorCooperativeLaunchTooLarge.doc: This error indicates that the number of blocks launched per grid for a kernel that was launched via either [cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EXECUTION.html#group__cudart__execution_1ga504b94170f83285c71031be6d5d15f73) exceeds the maximum number of blocks as allowed by [cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__OCCUPANCY.html#group__cudart__occupancy_1ga2d76683f563815291c065e958da2e7c2) or [cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessorWithFlags](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__OCCUPANCY.html#group__cudart__occupancy_1gae2255f3637784624ea99a6d3c7885ca0) times the number of multiprocessors as specified by the device attribute [cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga49e2f8c2c0bd6fe264f2fc970912e5cda74de9ed281f917c8e4ef272da09f338a).

cudaErrorCudartUnloading.doc: This indicates that a CUDA Runtime API call cannot be executed because it is being called during process shut down, at a point in time after CUDA driver has been unloaded.

cudaErrorDeviceAlreadyInUse.doc: This indicates that a call tried to access an exclusive-thread device that is already in use by a different thread.

cudaErrorDeviceNotLicensed.doc: This indicates that the device doesn’t have a valid Grid License.

cudaErrorDeviceUninitialized.doc:
This most frequently indicates that there is no context bound to the current thread.

This can also be returned if the context passed to an API call is not a valid handle (such as a context that has had ::cuCtxDestroy() invoked on it). This can also be returned if a user mixes different API versions (i.e. 3010 context with 3020 API calls). See ::cuCtxGetApiVersion() for more details.

cudaErrorDevicesUnavailable.doc:
This indicates that all CUDA devices are busy or unavailable at the current time.

Devices are often busy/unavailable due to use of [cudaComputeModeProhibited](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga7eb25f5413a962faad0956d92bae10d0afc71b88518e4501544d6e65b5f3671b6), [cudaComputeModeExclusiveProcess](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga7eb25f5413a962faad0956d92bae10d0a2cd032834fecbec513ea1018145b111d), or when long running CUDA kernels have filled up the GPU and are blocking new work from starting. They can also be unavailable due to memory constraints on a device that already has active CUDA work being performed.

cudaErrorDuplicateSurfaceName.doc: This indicates that multiple surfaces (across separate CUDA source files in the application) share the same string name.

cudaErrorDuplicateTextureName.doc: This indicates that multiple textures (across separate CUDA source files in the application) share the same string name.

cudaErrorDuplicateVariableName.doc: This indicates that multiple global or constant variables (across separate CUDA source files in the application) share the same string name.

cudaErrorECCUncorrectable.doc: This indicates that an uncorrectable ECC error was detected during execution.

cudaErrorExternalDevice.doc:
This indicates that an error has occurred in a device outside of GPU.

It can be a synchronous error with respect to CUDA API or an asynchronous error from the external device. In case of asynchronous error, it means that if CUDA was waiting for an external device’s signal before consuming shared data, the external device signaled an error indicating that the data is not valid for consumption. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched. In case of synchronous error, it means that one or more external devices have encountered an error and cannot complete the operation.

cudaErrorFabricNotReady.doc:
This error indicates GPU fabric is not ready within the bounded wait while the fabric manager probe is still in progress.

Applications may retry after a delay; for the initialization wait budget, see environment variables such as CUDA_FABRIC_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS.

cudaErrorFileNotFound.doc: This indicates that the file specified was not found.

cudaErrorFunctionNotLoaded.doc: Indiciates a function handle is not loaded when calling an API that requires a loaded function.

cudaErrorGraphExecUpdateFailure.doc: This error indicates that the graph update was not performed because it included changes which violated constraints specific to instantiated graph update.

cudaErrorGraphRecaptureFailure.doc: This error indicates that a graph recapture failed and had to be terminated.

cudaErrorHardwareStackError.doc:
Device encountered an error in the call stack during kernel execution, possibly due to stack corruption or exceeding the stack size limit.

This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorHostMemoryAlreadyRegistered.doc: This error indicates that the memory range passed to [cudaHostRegister()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1gae8d5c17670f16ac4fc8fcb4181cb490c) has already been registered.

cudaErrorHostMemoryNotRegistered.doc: This error indicates that the pointer passed to [cudaHostUnregister()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__MEMORY.html#group__cudart__memory_1ga81fd4101862bbefdb42a62d60e515eea) does not correspond to any currently registered memory region.

cudaErrorIllegalAddress.doc:
The device encountered a load or store instruction on an invalid memory address.

This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorIllegalInstruction.doc:
The device encountered an illegal instruction during kernel execution This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error.

To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorIllegalState.doc: This indicates that a resource required by the API call is not in a valid state to perform the requested operation.

cudaErrorIncompatibleDriverContext.doc:
This indicates that the current context is not compatible with this the CUDA Runtime.

This can only occur if you are using CUDA Runtime/Driver interoperability and have created an existing Driver context using the driver API. The Driver context may be incompatible either because the Driver context was created using an older version of the API, because the Runtime API call expects a primary driver context and the Driver context is not primary, or because the Driver context has been destroyed. Please see [Interactions](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DRIVER.html#group__cudart__driver) with the CUDA Driver API” for more information.

cudaErrorInitializationError.doc: The API call failed because the CUDA driver and runtime could not be initialized.

cudaErrorInsufficientDriver.doc:
This indicates that the installed NVIDIA CUDA driver is older than the CUDA runtime library.

This is not a supported configuration. Users should install an updated NVIDIA display driver to allow the application to run.

cudaErrorInsufficientLoaderVersion.doc: This indicates that loader version is insufficient for Fatbin.

cudaErrorInvalidAddressSpace.doc:
While executing a kernel, the device encountered an instruction which can only operate on memory locations in certain address spaces (global, shared, or local), but was supplied a memory address not belonging to an allowed address space.

This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorInvalidChannelDescriptor.doc:
This indicates that the channel descriptor passed to the API call is not valid.

This occurs if the format is not one of the formats specified by [cudaChannelFormatKind](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga8085eac5cb54b4228f3619a60f235119), or if one of the dimensions is invalid.

cudaErrorInvalidClusterSize.doc: This indicates that a kernel launch error has occurred due to cluster misconfiguration.

cudaErrorInvalidConfiguration.doc:
This indicates that a kernel launch is requesting resources that can never be satisfied by the current device.

Requesting more shared memory per block than the device supports will trigger this error, as will requesting too many threads or blocks. See [cudaDeviceProp](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/structcudaDeviceProp.html#structcudadeviceprop) for more device limitations.

cudaErrorInvalidDevice.doc: This indicates that the device ordinal supplied by the user does not correspond to a valid CUDA device or that the action requested is invalid for the specified device.

cudaErrorInvalidDeviceFunction.doc: The requested device function does not exist or is not compiled for the proper device architecture.

cudaErrorInvalidDevicePointer.doc: This indicates that at least one device pointer passed to the API call is not a valid device pointer.

cudaErrorInvalidFilterSetting.doc:
This indicates that a non-float texture was being accessed with linear filtering.

This is not supported by CUDA.

cudaErrorInvalidGraphicsContext.doc: This indicates an error with the OpenGL or DirectX context.

cudaErrorInvalidHostPointer.doc: This indicates that at least one host pointer passed to the API call is not a valid host pointer.

cudaErrorInvalidKernelImage.doc: This indicates that the device kernel image is invalid.

cudaErrorInvalidMemcpyDirection.doc: This indicates that the direction of the memcpy passed to the API call is not one of the types specified by [cudaMemcpyKind](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga18fa99055ee694244a270e4d5101e95b).

cudaErrorInvalidNormSetting.doc:
This indicates that an attempt was made to read an unsupported data type as a normalized float.

This is not supported by CUDA.

cudaErrorInvalidPc.doc:
The device encountered an invalid program counter.

This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorInvalidPitchValue.doc: This indicates that one or more of the pitch-related parameters passed to the API call is not within the acceptable range for pitch.

cudaErrorInvalidPtx.doc:
A PTX compilation failed.

The runtime may fall back to compiling PTX if an application does not contain a suitable binary for the current device.

cudaErrorInvalidResourceConfiguration.doc: This error indicates one or more resources are insufficient or non-applicable for the operation.

cudaErrorInvalidResourceHandle.doc:
This indicates that a resource handle passed to the API call was not valid.

Resource handles are opaque types like [cudaStream_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gae15d9c8b7a240312b533d6122558085a) and [cudaEvent_t](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gaea2f543a9fc0e52fe4ae712920fd1247).

cudaErrorInvalidResourceType.doc: This error indicates one or more resources passed in are not valid resource types for the operation.

cudaErrorInvalidSource.doc: This indicates that the device kernel source is invalid.

cudaErrorInvalidSurface.doc: This indicates that the surface passed to the API call is not a valid surface.

cudaErrorInvalidSymbol.doc: This indicates that the symbol name/identifier passed to the API call is not a valid name or identifier.

cudaErrorInvalidTexture.doc: This indicates that the texture passed to the API call is not a valid texture.

cudaErrorInvalidTextureBinding.doc:
This indicates that the texture binding is not valid.

This occurs if you call ::cudaGetTextureAlignmentOffset() with an unbound texture.

cudaErrorInvalidValue.doc: This indicates that one or more of the parameters passed to the API call is not within an acceptable range of values.

cudaErrorJitCompilationDisabled.doc:
This indicates that the JIT compilation was disabled.

The JIT compilation compiles PTX. The runtime may fall back to compiling PTX if an application does not contain a suitable binary for the current device.

cudaErrorJitCompilerNotFound.doc:
This indicates that the PTX JIT compiler library was not found.

The JIT Compiler library is used for PTX compilation. The runtime may fall back to compiling PTX if an application does not contain a suitable binary for the current device.

cudaErrorLaunchFailure.doc:
An exception occurred on the device while executing a kernel.

Common causes include dereferencing an invalid device pointer and accessing out of bounds shared memory. Less common cases can be system specific - more information about these cases can be found in the system specific user guide. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorLaunchFileScopedSurf.doc:
This error indicates that a grid launch did not occur because the kernel uses file-scoped surfaces which are unsupported by the device runtime.

Kernels launched via the device runtime only support surfaces created with the Surface Object API’s.

cudaErrorLaunchFileScopedTex.doc:
This error indicates that a grid launch did not occur because the kernel uses file-scoped textures which are unsupported by the device runtime.

Kernels launched via the device runtime only support textures created with the Texture Object API’s.

cudaErrorLaunchIncompatibleTexturing.doc: This error indicates a kernel launch that uses an incompatible texturing mode.

cudaErrorLaunchMaxDepthExceeded.doc: This error indicates that a device runtime grid launch did not occur because the depth of the child grid would exceed the maximum supported number of nested grid launches.

cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources.doc:
This indicates that a launch did not occur because it did not have appropriate resources.

Although this error is similar to [cudaErrorInvalidConfiguration](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038ad3934977826b2e1488dfeb7e0614e776), this error usually indicates that the user has attempted to pass too many arguments to the device kernel, or the kernel launch specifies too many threads for the kernel’s register count.

cudaErrorLaunchPendingCountExceeded.doc:
This error indicates that a device runtime grid launch failed because the launch would exceed the limit [cudaLimitDevRuntimePendingLaunchCount](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga4c4b34c054d383b0e9a63ab0ffc93651a18712cb05d2c3efaeea73afba823d916).

For this launch to proceed successfully, [cudaDeviceSetLimit](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga05956f16eaa47ef3a4efee84563ccb7d) must be called to set the [cudaLimitDevRuntimePendingLaunchCount](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga4c4b34c054d383b0e9a63ab0ffc93651a18712cb05d2c3efaeea73afba823d916) to be higher than the upper bound of outstanding launches that can be issued to the device runtime. Keep in mind that raising the limit of pending device runtime launches will require the runtime to reserve device memory that cannot be used for user allocations.

cudaErrorLaunchTimeout.doc:
This indicates that the device kernel took too long to execute.

This can only occur if timeouts are enabled - see the device attribute cudaDevAttrKernelExecTimeout for more information. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorLossyQuery.doc:
This indicates an attempt was made to introspect an object in a way that would discard semantically important information.

This is either due to the object using funtionality newer than the API version used to introspect it or omission of optional return arguments.

cudaErrorMapBufferObjectFailed.doc: This indicates that the buffer object could not be mapped.

cudaErrorMemoryAllocation.doc: The API call failed because it was unable to allocate enough memory or other resources to perform the requested operation.

cudaErrorMemoryValueTooLarge.doc: This indicated that an emulated device pointer exceeded the 32-bit address range.

cudaErrorMisalignedAddress.doc:
The device encountered a load or store instruction on a memory address which is not aligned.

This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorMissingConfiguration.doc: The device function being invoked (usually via [cudaLaunchKernel()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EXECUTION.html#group__cudart__execution_1ga5064cdf5d8e6741ace56fd8be951783c)) was not previously configured via the ::cudaConfigureCall() function.

cudaErrorMixedDeviceExecution.doc: Mixing of device and device emulation code was not allowed.

cudaErrorMpsClientTerminated.doc:
This error indicates that the MPS client has been terminated by the server.

To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorMpsConnectionFailed.doc: This error indicates that the MPS client failed to connect to the MPS control daemon or the MPS server.

cudaErrorMpsMaxClientsReached.doc: This error indicates that the hardware resources required to create MPS client have been exhausted.

cudaErrorMpsMaxConnectionsReached.doc: This error indicates the hardware resources required to device connections have been exhausted.

cudaErrorMpsRpcFailure.doc: This error indicates that the remote procedural call between the MPS server and the MPS client failed.

cudaErrorMpsServerNotReady.doc:
This error indicates that the MPS server is not ready to accept new MPS client requests.

This error can be returned when the MPS server is in the process of recovering from a fatal failure.

cudaErrorNoDevice.doc: This indicates that no CUDA-capable devices were detected by the installed CUDA driver.

cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice.doc:
This indicates that there is no kernel image available that is suitable for the device.

This can occur when a user specifies code generation options for a particular CUDA source file that do not include the corresponding device configuration.

cudaErrorNotMapped.doc: This indicates that a resource is not mapped.

cudaErrorNotMappedAsArray.doc: This indicates that a mapped resource is not available for access as an array.

cudaErrorNotMappedAsPointer.doc: This indicates that a mapped resource is not available for access as a pointer.

cudaErrorNotPermitted.doc: This error indicates the attempted operation is not permitted.

cudaErrorNotReady.doc:
This indicates that asynchronous operations issued previously have not completed yet.

This result is not actually an error, but must be indicated differently than [cudaSuccess](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038ae355f04607d824883b4a50662830d591) (which indicates completion). Calls that may return this value include [cudaEventQuery()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EVENT.html#group__cudart__event_1ga2bf738909b4a059023537eaa29d8a5b7) and [cudaStreamQuery()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__STREAM.html#group__cudart__stream_1ga2021adeb17905c7ec2a3c1bf125c5435).

cudaErrorNotSupported.doc: This error indicates the attempted operation is not supported on the current system or device.

cudaErrorNotYetImplemented.doc:
This indicates that the API call is not yet implemented.

Production releases of CUDA will never return this error.

cudaErrorNvlinkUncorrectable.doc: This indicates that an uncorrectable NVLink error was detected during the execution.

cudaErrorOperatingSystem.doc: This error indicates that an OS call failed.

cudaErrorPeerAccessAlreadyEnabled.doc: This error indicates that a call to [cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__PEER.html#group__cudart__peer_1ga2b0adabf90db37e5cfddc92cbb2589f3) is trying to re-enable peer addressing on from a context which has already had peer addressing enabled.

cudaErrorPeerAccessNotEnabled.doc: This error indicates that [cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__PEER.html#group__cudart__peer_1ga9663734ad02653207ad6836053bf572e) is trying to disable peer addressing which has not been enabled yet via [cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__PEER.html#group__cudart__peer_1ga2b0adabf90db37e5cfddc92cbb2589f3).

cudaErrorPeerAccessUnsupported.doc: This error indicates that P2P access is not supported across the given devices.

cudaErrorPriorLaunchFailure.doc:
This indicated that a previous kernel launch failed.

This was previously used for device emulation of kernel launches.

cudaErrorProfilerDisabled.doc:
This indicates profiler is not initialized for this run.

This can happen when the application is running with external profiling tools like visual profiler.

cudaErrorSetOnActiveProcess.doc:
This indicates that the user has called [cudaSetValidDevices()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga1b9336c70f2299405f67a4f8496d7cfe), [cudaSetDeviceFlags()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga69e73c7dda3fc05306ae7c811a690fac), [cudaD3D9SetDirect3DDevice()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__D3D9.html#group__cudart__d3d9_1ga0733a6f0bdc8aca6c6812da66c6d814a), [cudaD3D10SetDirect3DDevice](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__D3D10__DEPRECATED.html#group__cudart__d3d10__deprecated_1gaec213424a812636fc03d48442caacea2), [cudaD3D11SetDirect3DDevice()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__D3D11__DEPRECATED.html#group__cudart__d3d11__deprecated_1ga1d65c1bdcbdd4d0d70e8c9c8a32f38ff), or [cudaVDPAUSetVDPAUDevice()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__VDPAU.html#group__cudart__vdpau_1ga2a9ccfe8e6c87fe694bafd8cfcc67586) after initializing the CUDA runtime by calling non-device management operations (allocating memory and launching kernels are examples of non-device management operations).

This error can also be returned if using runtime/driver interoperability and there is an existing ::CUcontext active on the host thread.

cudaErrorSharedObjectInitFailed.doc: This indicates that initialization of a shared object failed.

cudaErrorSharedObjectSymbolNotFound.doc: This indicates that a link to a shared object failed to resolve.

cudaErrorSoftwareValidityNotEstablished.doc:
By default, the CUDA runtime may perform a minimal set of self-tests, as well as CUDA driver tests, to establish the validity of both.

Introduced in CUDA 11.2, this error return indicates that at least one of these tests has failed and the validity of either the runtime or the driver could not be established.

cudaErrorStartupFailure.doc: This indicates an internal startup failure in the CUDA runtime.

cudaErrorStreamCaptureImplicit.doc: The operation would have resulted in a disallowed implicit dependency on a current capture sequence from cudaStreamLegacy.

cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated.doc: The current capture sequence on the stream has been invalidated due to a previous error.

cudaErrorStreamCaptureIsolation.doc:
A dependency would have been created which crosses the capture sequence boundary.

Only implicit in-stream ordering dependencies are allowed to cross the boundary.

cudaErrorStreamCaptureMerge.doc: The operation would have resulted in a merge of two independent capture sequences.

cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnjoined.doc: The capture sequence contains a fork that was not joined to the primary stream.

cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnmatched.doc: The capture was not initiated in this stream.

cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported.doc: The operation is not permitted when the stream is capturing.

cudaErrorStreamCaptureWrongThread.doc: A stream capture sequence not initiated with the cudaStreamCaptureModeRelaxed argument to [cudaStreamBeginCapture](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__STREAM.html#group__cudart__stream_1ga793d7d4e474388ddfda531603dc34aa3) was passed to [cudaStreamEndCapture](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__STREAM.html#group__cudart__stream_1gaf5a0efebc818054ceecd1e3e5e76d93e) in a different thread.

cudaErrorStreamDetached.doc:
This error indicates that the requested operation is not permitted because the stream is in a detached state.

This can occur if the green context associated with the stream has been destroyed, limiting the stream’s operational capabilities.

cudaErrorStubLibrary.doc:
This indicates that the CUDA driver that the application has loaded is a stub library.

Applications that run with the stub rather than a real driver loaded will result in CUDA API returning this error.

cudaErrorSymbolNotFound.doc:
This indicates that a named symbol was not found.

Examples of symbols are global/constant variable names, driver function names, texture names, and surface names.

cudaErrorSyncDepthExceeded.doc:
This error indicates that a call to [cudaDeviceSynchronize](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga096cfe1b3923b1932ef4af405ec7c1b9) made from the device runtime failed because the call was made at grid depth greater than than either the default (2 levels of grids) or user specified device limit [cudaLimitDevRuntimeSyncDepth](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga4c4b34c054d383b0e9a63ab0ffc93651a23c4900be4af436cb769e4c72d07be11).

To be able to synchronize on launched grids at a greater depth successfully, the maximum nested depth at which [cudaDeviceSynchronize](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga096cfe1b3923b1932ef4af405ec7c1b9) will be called must be specified with the [cudaLimitDevRuntimeSyncDepth](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga4c4b34c054d383b0e9a63ab0ffc93651a23c4900be4af436cb769e4c72d07be11) limit to the [cudaDeviceSetLimit](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga05956f16eaa47ef3a4efee84563ccb7d) api before the host-side launch of a kernel using the device runtime. Keep in mind that additional levels of sync depth require the runtime to reserve large amounts of device memory that cannot be used for user allocations. Note that [cudaDeviceSynchronize](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga096cfe1b3923b1932ef4af405ec7c1b9) made from device runtime is only supported on devices of compute capability < 9.0.

cudaErrorSynchronizationError.doc:
This indicated that a synchronization operation had failed.

This was previously used for some device emulation functions.

cudaErrorSystemDriverMismatch.doc:
This error indicates that there is a mismatch between the versions of the display driver and the CUDA driver.

Refer to the compatibility documentation for supported versions.

cudaErrorSystemNotReady.doc:
This error indicates that the system is not yet ready to start any CUDA work.

To continue using CUDA, verify the system configuration is in a valid state and all required driver daemons are actively running. More information about this error can be found in the system specific user guide.

cudaErrorTensorMemoryLeak.doc:
An exception occurred on the device while exiting a kernel using tensor memory: the tensor memory was not completely deallocated.

This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

cudaErrorTextureFetchFailed.doc:
This indicated that a texture fetch was not able to be performed.

This was previously used for device emulation of texture operations.

cudaErrorTextureNotBound.doc:
This indicated that a texture was not bound for access.

This was previously used for device emulation of texture operations.

cudaErrorTimeout.doc: This indicates that the wait operation has timed out.

cudaErrorTooManyPeers.doc: This error indicates that the hardware resources required to enable peer access have been exhausted for one or more of the devices passed to ::cudaEnablePeerAccess().

cudaErrorUnknown.doc: This indicates that an unknown internal error has occurred.

cudaErrorUnmapBufferObjectFailed.doc: This indicates that the buffer object could not be unmapped.

cudaErrorUnsupportedDevSideSync.doc: This indicates that the code to be compiled by the PTX JIT contains unsupported call to cudaDeviceSynchronize.

cudaErrorUnsupportedExecAffinity.doc: This indicates that the provided execution affinity is not supported by the device.

cudaErrorUnsupportedLimit.doc: This indicates that the [cudaLimit](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga4c4b34c054d383b0e9a63ab0ffc93651) passed to the API call is not supported by the active device.

cudaErrorUnsupportedPtxVersion.doc:
This indicates that the provided PTX was compiled with an unsupported toolchain.

The most common reason for this, is the PTX was generated by a compiler newer than what is supported by the CUDA driver and PTX JIT compiler.

cudaErrorVersionTranslation.doc: This indicates that the driver is newer than the runtime version and returned graph node parameter information that the runtime does not understand and is unable to translate.

cudaExternalMemoryHandleTypeD3D11Resourc.doc: Handle is a shared NT handle to a D3D11 resource.
Handle is a globally shared handle to a D3D11 resource.

cudaExternalMemoryHandleTypeD3D12Heap.doc: Handle is a D3D12 heap object.

cudaExternalMemoryHandleTypeD3D12Resourc.doc: Handle is a D3D12 committed resource.

cudaExternalMemoryHandleTypeOpaqueFd.doc: Handle is an opaque file descriptor.

cudaExternalMemoryHandleTypeOpaqueWin32.doc: Handle is an opaque shared NT handle.

cudaExternalMemoryHandleTypeOpaqueWin32K.doc: Handle is an opaque, globally shared handle.

cudaExternalSemaphoreHandleTypeD3D11Fenc.doc: Handle is a shared NT handle referencing a D3D11 fence object.

cudaExternalSemaphoreHandleTypeD3D12Fenc.doc: Handle is a shared NT handle referencing a D3D12 fence object.

cudaExternalSemaphoreHandleTypeKeyedMute.doc: Handle is a shared NT handle referencing a D3D11 keyed mutex object.
Handle is a shared KMT handle referencing a D3D11 keyed mutex object.

cudaExternalSemaphoreHandleTypeOpaqueFd.doc: Handle is an opaque file descriptor.

cudaExternalSemaphoreHandleTypeOpaqueWin.doc: Handle is an opaque shared NT handle.
Handle is an opaque, globally shared handle.

cudaExternalSemaphoreHandleTypeTimelineS.doc: Handle is an opaque handle file descriptor referencing a timeline semaphore.
Handle is an opaque handle file descriptor referencing a timeline semaphore.

cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesOptionHost.doc: [cudaDeviceFlushGPUDirectRDMAWrites()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga3fc2853f4f30ce29019a8db822354d12) and its CUDA Driver API counterpart are supported on the device.

cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesOptionMemOps.doc: The ::CU_STREAM_WAIT_VALUE_FLUSH flag and the ::CU_STREAM_MEM_OP_FLUSH_REMOTE_WRITES MemOp are supported on the CUDA device.

cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesTargetCurren.doc: Sets the target for [cudaDeviceFlushGPUDirectRDMAWrites()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__DEVICE.html#group__cudart__device_1ga3fc2853f4f30ce29019a8db822354d12) to the currently active CUDA device context.

cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesToAllDevices.doc: Blocks until remote writes are visible to all CUDA device contexts.

cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWritesToOwner.doc: Blocks until remote writes are visible to the CUDA device context owning the data.

cudaFuncAttributeClusterDimMustBeSet.doc: Indicator to enforce valid cluster dimension specification on kernel launch.

cudaFuncAttributeNonPortableClusterSizeA.doc: Whether non-portable cluster scheduling policy is supported.

cudaFuncAttributeSharedMemoryMode.doc: Setting that controls a kernel’s use of non-portable or oversized shared memory configurations.

cudaFuncCachePreferEqual.doc: Prefer equal size L1 cache and shared memory.

cudaFuncCachePreferL1.doc: Prefer larger L1 cache and smaller shared memory.

cudaFuncCachePreferNone.doc: Default function cache configuration, no preference.

cudaFuncCachePreferShared.doc: Prefer larger shared memory and smaller L1 cache.

cudaGLDeviceListAll.doc: The CUDA devices for all GPUs used by the current OpenGL context.

cudaGLDeviceListCurrentFrame.doc: The CUDA devices for the GPUs used by the current OpenGL context in its currently rendering frame.

cudaGLDeviceListNextFrame.doc: The CUDA devices for the GPUs to be used by the current OpenGL context in the next frame.

cudaGLMapFlagsNone.doc: Default; Assume resource can be read/written.

cudaGLMapFlagsReadOnly.doc: CUDA kernels will not write to this resource.

cudaGLMapFlagsWriteDiscard.doc: CUDA kernels will only write to and will not read from this resource.

cudaGPUDirectRDMAWritesOrderingAllDevice.doc: Any CUDA device in the system can consistently consume GPUDirect RDMA writes to this device.

cudaGPUDirectRDMAWritesOrderingNone.doc:
The device does not natively support ordering of GPUDirect RDMA writes.

::cudaFlushGPUDirectRDMAWrites() can be leveraged if supported.

cudaGPUDirectRDMAWritesOrderingOwner.doc: Natively, the device can consistently consume GPUDirect RDMA writes, although other CUDA devices may not.

cudaGraphChildGraphOwnershipClone.doc:
Default behavior for a child graph node.

Child graph is cloned into the parent and memory allocation/free nodes can’t be present in the child graph.

cudaGraphChildGraphOwnershipInvalid.doc:
Invalid ownership flag.

Set when params are queried to prevent accidentally reusing the driver-owned graph object.

cudaGraphChildGraphOwnershipMove.doc:
The child graph is moved to the parent.

The handle to the child graph is owned by the parent and will be destroyed when the parent is destroyed.

The following restrictions apply to child graphs after they have been moved: Cannot be independently instantiated or destroyed; Cannot be added as a child graph of a separate parent graph; Cannot be used as an argument to cudaGraphExecUpdate; Cannot have additional memory allocation or free nodes added.

cudaGraphCondAssignDefault.doc: Apply default handle value when graph is launched.

cudaGraphCondTypeIf.doc:
Conditional ‘if/else’ Node.

Body[0] executed if condition is non-zero. If `size` == 2, an optional ELSE graph is created and this is executed if the condition is zero.

cudaGraphCondTypeSwitch.doc:
Conditional ‘switch’ Node.

Body[n] is executed once, where ‘n’ is the value of the condition. If the condition does not match a body index, no body is launched.

cudaGraphCondTypeWhile.doc:
Conditional ‘while’ Node.

Body executed repeatedly while condition value is non-zero.

cudaGraphDebugDotFlagsEventNodeParams.doc: Adds cudaEvent_t handle from record and wait nodes to output.

cudaGraphDebugDotFlagsHandles.doc: Adds node handles and every kernel function handle to output.

cudaGraphDebugDotFlagsVerbose.doc: Output all debug data as if every debug flag is enabled.

cudaGraphDependencyTypeProgrammatic.doc:
This dependency type allows the downstream node to use `cudaGridDependencySynchronize()`.

It may only be used between kernel nodes, and must be used with either the [cudaGraphKernelNodePortProgrammatic](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga54b3445f86974c1ddeccb3cea9d7b06c) or [cudaGraphKernelNodePortLaunchCompletion](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga815c9c164c4679d738445d3b56b5bfc4) outgoing port.

cudaGraphExecUpdateError.doc: The update failed for an unexpected reason which is described in the return value of the function.

cudaGraphExecUpdateErrorAttributesChange.doc: The update failed because the node attributes changed in a way that is not supported.

cudaGraphExecUpdateErrorFunctionChanged.doc: The update failed because the function of a kernel node changed (CUDA driver < 11.2).

cudaGraphExecUpdateErrorNodeTypeChanged.doc: The update failed because a node type changed.

cudaGraphExecUpdateErrorNotSupported.doc: The update failed because something about the node is not supported.

cudaGraphExecUpdateErrorParametersChange.doc: The update failed because the parameters changed in a way that is not supported.

cudaGraphExecUpdateErrorTopologyChanged.doc: The update failed because the topology changed.

cudaGraphExecUpdateErrorUnsupportedFunct.doc: The update failed because the function of a kernel node changed in an unsupported way.

cudaGraphInstantiateConditionalHandleUnu.doc: One or more conditional handles are not associated with conditional nodes.

cudaGraphInstantiateError.doc: Instantiation failed for an unexpected reason which is described in the return value of the function.

cudaGraphInstantiateFlagAutoFreeOnLaunch.doc: Automatically free memory allocated in a graph before relaunching.

cudaGraphInstantiateFlagDeviceLaunch.doc:
Instantiate the graph to be launchable from the device.

This flag can only

be used on platforms which support unified addressing. This flag cannot be.

cudaGraphInstantiateFlagUpload.doc:
Automatically upload the graph after instantiation.

Only supported by [cudaGraphInstantiateWithParams](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__GRAPH.html#group__cudart__graph_1ga49739708386dc6da9603eb7cc5557db4)

. The upload will be performed using the

stream provided in.

cudaGraphInstantiateFlagUseNodePriority.doc: Run the graph using the per-node priority attributes rather than the priority of the stream it is launched into.

cudaGraphInstantiateInvalidStructure.doc: Instantiation failed due to invalid structure, such as cycles.

cudaGraphInstantiateMultipleDevicesNotSu.doc: Instantiation for device launch failed due to the nodes belonging to different contexts.

cudaGraphInstantiateNodeOperationNotSupp.doc: Instantiation for device launch failed because the graph contained an unsupported operation.

cudaGraphMemAttrReservedMemCurrent.doc: (value type = cuuint64_t) Amount of memory, in bytes, currently allocated for use by the CUDA graphs asynchronous allocator.

cudaGraphMemAttrReservedMemHigh.doc: (value type = cuuint64_t) High watermark of memory, in bytes, currently allocated for use by the CUDA graphs asynchronous allocator.

cudaGraphMemAttrUsedMemCurrent.doc: (value type = cuuint64_t) Amount of memory, in bytes, currently associated with graphs.

cudaGraphMemAttrUsedMemHigh.doc:
(value type = cuuint64_t) High watermark of memory, in bytes, associated with graphs since the last time it was reset.

High watermark can only be reset to zero.

cudaGraphNodeTypeGraph.doc: Node which executes an embedded graph.

cudaGraphRecaptureEligibleForUpdate.doc: Node is eligible for update in an instantiated graph.

cudaGraphRecaptureError.doc:
Error while attempting to recapture the node.

The recapture will be ended regardless of the return value from the callback.

cudaGraphRecaptureIneligibleForUpdate.doc: Parameter changes in the node cannot be applied to an instantiated graph.

cudaGraphUserObjectMove.doc: Transfer references from the caller rather than creating new references.

cudaGraphicsMapFlagsNone.doc: Default; Assume resource can be read/written.

cudaGraphicsMapFlagsReadOnly.doc: CUDA will not write to this resource.

cudaGraphicsMapFlagsWriteDiscard.doc: CUDA will only write to and will not read from this resource.

cudaGraphicsRegisterFlagsReadOnly.doc: CUDA will not write to this resource.

cudaGraphicsRegisterFlagsSurfaceLoadStor.doc: CUDA will bind this resource to a surface reference.

cudaGraphicsRegisterFlagsTextureGather.doc: CUDA will perform texture gather operations on this resource.

cudaGraphicsRegisterFlagsWriteDiscard.doc: CUDA will only write to and will not read from this resource.

cudaJitCacheMode.doc:
Specifies whether to enable caching explicitly (-dlcm)

Choice is based on supplied

Option type: unsigned int for enumerated type [cudaJit_CacheMode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga0c8956e7ff8d9e622b4e109355a4b68b)
Applies to: compiler only.

cudaJitErrorLogBufferSizeBytes.doc:
IN: Log buffer size in bytes.

Log messages will be capped at this size (including null terminator)

OUT: Amount of log buffer filled with messages

Option type: unsigned int

Applies to: compiler and linker.

cudaJitFallbackStrategy.doc:
Specifies choice of fallback strategy if matching cubin is not found.

Choice is based on supplied [cudaJit_Fallback](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga9ce78a9663fa9247c95dbbced82b62b7). Option type: unsigned int for enumerated type [cudaJit_Fallback](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga9ce78a9663fa9247c95dbbced82b62b7)
Applies to: compiler only.

cudaJitGenerateDebugInfo.doc:
Specifies whether to create debug information in output (-g) (0: false, default)

Option type: int.

cudaJitGenerateLineInfo.doc:
Generate line number information (-lineinfo) (0: false, default)

Option type: int.

cudaJitInfoLogBufferSizeBytes.doc:
IN: Log buffer size in bytes.

Log messages will be capped at this size (including null terminator)

OUT: Amount of log buffer filled with messages

Option type: unsigned int

Applies to: compiler and linker.

cudaJitLogVerbose.doc:
Generate verbose log messages (0: false, default)

Option type: int.

cudaJitMaxRegisters.doc:
Max number of registers that a thread may use.

Option type: unsigned int

Applies to: compiler only.

cudaJitMaxThreadsPerBlock.doc:
Maximum number threads in a thread block, computed as the product of the maximum extent specifed for each dimension of the block.

This limit is guaranteed not to be exeeded in any invocation of the kernel. Exceeding the maximum number of threads results in runtime error or kernel launch failure. For kernels already using PTX directive .maxntid, this option will be ignored by default. Use [cudaJitOverrideDirectiveValues](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga5516e6d5c1b78ac4cb26c203ade11484ac976ec67f91d8af12d05f775c4b0cda3)

to let this option take precedence over the PTX directive. Option type: int

Applies to: compiler only.

cudaJitMinCtaPerSm.doc:
This option hints to the JIT compiler the minimum number of CTAs from the kernel’s grid to be mapped to a SM.

This option is ignored when used together with [cudaJitMaxRegisters](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga5516e6d5c1b78ac4cb26c203ade11484ae3038d5cfc098594db548c404332a8fa) or [cudaJitThreadsPerBlock](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga5516e6d5c1b78ac4cb26c203ade11484ac6bd437b08e74ea5ed30288cea49c00f). Optimizations based on this option need [cudaJitMaxThreadsPerBlock](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga5516e6d5c1b78ac4cb26c203ade11484aedcd620933228c98c95edd6c9b554de0) to be specified as well. For kernels already using PTX directive .minnctapersm, this option will be ignored by default. Use [cudaJitOverrideDirectiveValues](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga5516e6d5c1b78ac4cb26c203ade11484ac976ec67f91d8af12d05f775c4b0cda3)

to let this option take precedence over the PTX directive. Option type: unsigned int

Applies to: compiler only.

cudaJitOptimizationLevel.doc:
Level of optimizations to apply to generated code (0 - 4), with 4 being the default and highest level of optimizations.

Option type: unsigned int

Applies to: compiler only.

cudaJitOverrideDirectiveValues.doc:

cudaLaunchAttributeNvlinkUtilCentricSche.doc:
Valid for streams, graph nodes, launches.

This attribute is a hint to the CUDA runtime that the launch should attempt to make the kernel maximize its NVLINK utilization.

When possible to honor this hint, CUDA will assume each block in the grid launch will carry out an even amount of NVLINK traffic, and make a best-effort attempt to adjust the kernel launch based on that assumption.

This attribute is a hint only. CUDA makes no functional or performance guarantee. Its applicability can be affected by many different factors, including driver version (i.e. CUDA doesn’t guarantee the performance characteristics will be maintained between driver versions or a driver update could alter or regress previously observed perf characteristics.) It also doesn’t guarantee a successful result, i.e. applying the attribute may not improve the performance of either the targeted kernel or the encapsulating application.

cudaLaunchAttributePortableClusterSizeMo.doc:
Valid for graph nodes, launches.

This indicates whether the kernel launch is allowed to use a non-portable cluster size. Valid values for [cudaLaunchAttributeValue::portableClusterSizeMode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/unioncudaLaunchAttributeValue.html#unioncudalaunchattributevalue_1a36a3fac80c29bafc05cda73b5071e7a6) are values for [cudaLaunchAttributePortableClusterMode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ga567a01dbf2ad07630a3943c2dfd04248) Any other value will return [cudaErrorInvalidValue](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1gga3f51e3575c2178246db0a94a430e0038a3e8aef5398ee38e28ed41e357b48917c).

cudaLaunchAttributePreferredClusterDimen.doc:
Valid for graph nodes and launches.

Set [cudaLaunchAttributeValue::preferredClusterDim](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/unioncudaLaunchAttributeValue.html#unioncudalaunchattributevalue_1aac671df7c302681278c372743a4f242e) to allow the kernel launch to specify a preferred substitute cluster dimension. Blocks may be grouped according to either the dimensions specified with this attribute (grouped into a “preferred substitute cluster”), or the one specified with [cudaLaunchAttributeClusterDimension](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ggafc5ed48085f05863b1aeebb14934b056a3de2ec80489ee6a8010335db69abc3ff)

attribute (grouped into a “regular cluster”). The cluster dimensions of a “preferred substitute cluster” shall be an integer multiple greater than zero of the regular cluster dimensions. The device will attempt - on a best-effort basis - to group thread blocks into preferred clusters over grouping them into regular clusters. When it deems necessary (primarily when the device temporarily runs out of physical resources to launch the larger preferred clusters), the device may switch to launch the regular clusters instead to attempt to utilize as much of the physical device resources as possible.

Each type of cluster will have its enumeration / coordinate setup as if the grid consists solely of its type of cluster. For example, if the preferred substitute cluster dimensions double the regular cluster dimensions, there might be simultaneously a regular cluster indexed at (1,0,0), and a preferred cluster indexed at (1,0,0). In this example, the preferred substitute cluster (1,0,0) replaces regular clusters (2,0,0) and (3,0,0) and groups their blocks.

cudaLaunchAttributePreferredSharedMemory.doc:
Valid for launches.

On devices where the L1 cache and shared memory use the same hardware resources, setting [cudaLaunchAttributeValue::sharedMemCarveout](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/unioncudaLaunchAttributeValue.html#unioncudalaunchattributevalue_1a5b20c278c86e5f0cfb34cd91c70c1bdd) to a percentage between 0-100 signals sets the shared memory carveout preference in percent of the total shared memory for that kernel launch. This attribute takes precedence over [cudaFuncAttributePreferredSharedMemoryCarveout](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__cudart__types_1ggac6c537b33d22c871a103f0fda8ac8bbead410365fab79998b26bf68000cac7194). cudaLaunchAttributeProgrammaticEvent.doc:
Valid for launches.

Set [cudaLaunchAttributeValue::programmaticEvent](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/unioncudaLaunchAttributeValue.html#unioncudalaunchattributevalue_1ad53249ac5e1d0f756abdbc2b2b1f42b1) to record the event. Event recorded through this launch attribute is guaranteed to only trigger after all block in the associated kernel trigger the event. A block can trigger the event programmatically in a future CUDA release. A trigger can also be inserted at the beginning of each block’s execution if triggerAtBlockStart is set to non-0. The dependent launches can choose to wait on the dependency using the programmatic sync ([cudaGridDependencySynchronize()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EXECUTION.html#group__cudart__execution_1ga9057f99234a8311c4c5d426cd501d99d) or equivalent PTX instructions). Note that dependents (including the CPU thread calling [cudaEventSynchronize()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EVENT.html#group__cudart__event_1ga949aa42b30ae9e622f6ba0787129ff22)) are not guaranteed to observe the release precisely when it is released. For example, [cudaEventSynchronize()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EVENT.html#group__cudart__event_1ga949aa42b30ae9e622f6ba0787129ff22)

may only observe the event trigger long after the associated kernel has completed. This recording type is primarily meant for establishing programmatic dependency between device tasks. Note also this type of dependency allows, but does not guarantee, concurrent execution of tasks.

The event supplied must not be an interprocess or interop event. The event must disable timing (i.e. must be created with the.

cudaLaunchAttributeProgrammaticStreamSer.doc:

cudaSuccess.doc:
The API call returned with no errors.

In the case of query calls, this also means that the operation being queried is complete (see [cudaEventQuery()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__EVENT.html#group__cudart__event_1ga2bf738909b4a059023537eaa29d8a5b7) and [cudaStreamQuery()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.4.2/cuda-runtime-api/cuda_runtime_api/group__CUDART__STREAM.html#group__cudart__stream_1ga2021adeb17905c7ec2a3c1bf125c5435)).

cudaUserObjectNoDestructorSync.doc: Indicates the destructor execution is not synchronized by any CUDA handle.
